newsitem.title: USA: Warm temperatures boost Minnesota crop development.
newsitem.headline: Warm temperatures boost Minnesota crop development.

text.p: Above normal temperatures aided Minnesota corn and soybean development in the week ended Sunday, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly update.
The percentage of corn dented increased to 46 percent this week, up from 13 percent the previous week but trailing the five-year average of 56 percent.
Corn was rated three percent very poor, eight percent poor, 39 fair, 42 percent good and eight percent excellent.
Soybeans were rated three percent very poor, eight percent poor, 40 fair, 45 good and four percent excellent.
Ten percent of the soybean crop had begun shedding leaves, against the five-year average of 12 percent.
Sugarbeet lifting had begun and the crop was rated two percent poor, 18 fair, 68 good and 12 percent excellent.
Two percent of the crop had been harvested.
Topsoil moisture was rated 22 percent very short, 34 percent short, 41 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
Pasture and range were rated 15 percent very poor, 24 percent poor, 38 percent fair, 22 percent good and one percent excellent.
